component.name: Modula
component.summary: A broadcast radio receiver for RTL-SDR dongles

description.p: Modula turns an RTL-SDR dongle into an FM and AM radio. It shows a frequency and a volume knob, not a signal-processing panel: there is no demodulator, filter or gain to choose, because none of them has a right answer a listener should have to supply.

ul.li: FM stereo, with a blend that narrows a weak station's image rather than dropping it to mono
RDS station names, radio text and programme type
Seek in either direction, and presets
A spectrum strip showing the station between its neighbours
Medium-wave and airband AM where the hardware reaches them
Recording, immediately or on a schedule

description.p: It drives the dongle directly through librtlsdr, or a dongle on another machine over rtl_tcp.

screenshot.caption: Tuned to an FM station in stereo, with the spectrum strip and four presets

description.p: Stereo decodes correctly on real transmitters, RDS keeps what stations send, and the keyboard keeps working after a click. The installers carry their licences, and the Linux package installs on Debian 12 and Ubuntu 22.04.
Daylight reaches the standard controls, a station on the weak-signal threshold no longer restyles the dial, and an ADC headroom readout says when more gain would clip.
No more dropped samples on the USB path, a steady stereo indicator, fixed gain instead of two AGCs, a stereo blend for weak stations and a quieting figure in the status line.
The first release: FM stereo with RDS, AM, seek, presets, recording and the tray.
